title: Valley
text: A very enjoyable game. Excellent atmosphere and environments, well realised. (The concept art work at the end credits is worth checking out too.) The story isn't Earth-shattering (excuse the pun), but is well told and sufficiently engaging. There are notes scattered about if you care to read more into the story, but the majority is (very well) voice-acted in-game while continuing to play. This means there are no flow-breaking cutscenes, which was an excellent choice here; far more immersive. I thought the game length was ideal for the price. It felt varied, complete and rewarding. Without outstaying its welcome or intruducing 'padding' just for the sake of making the game longer. It's certainly not a challenging game; yet I still felt involved enough to play all the way through before I realised this. On the negatives side, there were a couple of places where it was really unclear what to do; which were inevitably game-blocking. This in not unusual in this kind of game, and it's probably better than never feeling that you actually had to contribute something to progress. Also, there is no save feature; instead checkpoints are used. This actually works really well while playing; being able to save before every single action would probably break the game considerably. The problem comes when you have to stop playing (yes; some of us do ;). Then you can only re-start and the beginning of the entire area, potentially losing considerable progress. A final negative is that I didn't enjoy the in-door sections nearly as much as being outside. Unfortunately, the majority of the game seemed to be played in some kind of 'facility' or another. Making far too little use of the tititular 'Valley' imo. Overall though the game's negatives were insignificant compared to its appeal. Not many games hold my attention right until the end, but this definitely did. Highly recommended.

title: Valley
text: Valley is an absolutely enchanting experience. The story is very interesting and kept me engaged from start to finish. Exploring Valley was very rewarding and memorable due to the awesome L.E.A.F. suit you acquire at the start of the game. This allows you to build up huge momentum as you run down hills or speed through underground tunnels on electrified rails. The various upgrades found as you complete the story add additional functions like a grappling hook (which is context sensitive unfortuantely), double jump, magnetic wall climbing, and water running. There is also a bit of an FPS element as you will need to use the suits ability to fire energy blasts to defeat enemies. The energy consumed for attacks is also your health and can be replenished by draining it from plants, animals, and generators. However if you drain too many animals and trees the health of the valley itself is lowered, if this reaches zero the game ends. Where Valley really shines is it's story and freedom of movement as you explore each beautiful area in search of secrets such as upgrades for the suits energy capacity. Once you have completed the main story you can revisit each area to hunt down any remaining secrets, there is a completion percentage shown for each level so you will know right away if you missed anything. The voice work and music are excellent throughout as was the overall performance, I did not encounter any major glitches or frame rate issues. Valley is an easy recommendation if you just want to relax and explore a fantastic environment while unraveling a mysterious story. Be aware that Valley is very light on the combat and the only real challenge comes from platforming as there aren't really any puzzles.

title: Vikings - Wolves of Midgard
text: Is this the best game ever? No. Is it a good game? Yes. It's fun to play. Is it worth 40 bucks? It depends on what you like. It's pretty nice with the action and strategy involved in this game, along with the hot keys/abilities. For example in the area before the 2nd boss I encountered some mobs with large shields. How is that special? Well, in this game the shield actually works.. If you are attacking from the way the mob is facing you, you have a high chance of hitting the enemy's shield instead of the enemy. In addition to this you are dodging by using WSAD to roll different directions (the controls are sweet as well). And on top of this you can use 1-5 for example to throw fire, etc. (or whatever other abilities you chose each level). There is also some mode where waves of mobs come at you; I just tried the 1st one, and it was pretty cool. And all of this adds up to FUN. :) How's the frame rate? I don't keep track of that, but I can tell you in the first two acts I haven't received any lag, and the graphics are pretty nice. The mob variety is pretty good, and they all look pretty good. The armor drops I received were ok. I believe there is some randomness to armor drops, but not sure how much. I would say so far drops are no where near like games like Diablo 3, etc. There are a decent amount of hidden treasures around though. And the drops you get you can sell to get materials/gold which you use to upgrade armor/weapons, and the smith and weapon person. There are also some good weapons/armor drops as well. EDIT: Also one cool feature: you can go back to areas you previously completed with quests AND enemies all respawn in that area (I'm guessing they are all the same enemies though). The  rewards you get are gold and crafting materials from what I've seen so far which are used to upgrade your smith, etc. in the main hub. You may be asking why you've seem some negative review possibly? The way leading up to the 1st boss has a lot of similiar mobs and takes a while to get through, so as a result you will have people giving quick reviews that played 2 hours or less and didn't get to see much.In addition another big factor for some is it's not easy. I was playing on normal and died to the 1st boss several times. What did I do? I went back to town and crafted some better gear, and then I reran that area. The game hits the sweet spot imo on challenge on normal mode. I haven't tried online yet, so I cannot comment on that portion of the game. The controls are good: left mouse button to move/attack, right mouse can dodge, WSAD can dodge in different directions, 1-5 are abilities, tab is heal, etc. And yes the controls are customizable (except I don't think the mouse buttons are except for a few options). I like game slike Titan's Quest, Diablo 3, Grim Dawn, Torchlight 2, etc. This game has some elements from most of those games, but it doesn't have everything. One thing that makes this game special though is the action/strategy involved along with the mob variety. So if that intrigues you, I'd say go for it. Replayability? I'd say the action, strategy, abilities, respawning enemies from areas you completed previously, etc. will keep me coming back. In addition this is one of thos games where I'd say support the developers and they may build on this game in the future with possible expansions, etc.

title: Vikings - Wolves of Midgard
text: Vikings: Wolves of Midgard is a hard game to recommend. But I've played more than 20 hours of it and mostly enjoyed my time with it, so recommended it I will. Know, though, that it's very rough, with many questionable design decisions and an overall... lack of ambition is maybe not the right way to put it, since a lot of work was put into it and it shows, but let's say it doesn't set its sights particularly high. The TLDR version would be to get this in a sale if you like ARPGs, and not at all if you don't care for them. What it is is an action RPG, with an emphasis on the action. You play as the leader of the most shiftless tribe of vikings (Wolves of Midgard(tm)) ever commited to game. As such, you're forced to venture out on missions to single-handedly save their sorry arses while they stay back and do nothing. Which sounds historically accurate to me; I don't remember Hagar the viking (not a Wolf of Midgard, as far as I know) ever actually doing anything. So you're basically fighting to preserve the viking (Wolves of Midgard(tm)) way of life. Your character will even bemoan this lack of support, which is a slightly amusing and a whole lot aggravating. This practice is called lampshading and it's just... basically trying to cover up a shoddy aspect of something by calling attention to it for humorous effect. Instead of, you know, trying to do something about it. Ugh. Anyhow! So you use your tribe's hometown as a base hub (with traders, crafters and all the amenities) and launch incursions into discrete levels that function as either story missions or simply raids for experience and loot. It evolves over time, which is a neat touch - I really liked how your hall slowly fills with trophies from vanquished bosses. The maps you go a-viking to are simple but sprawling, with a decent amount of variety in both environments and enemies to fight, and some secrets to reward exploration, and they always end in some form of boss fight. There's always a story mission available, though sometimes they'll be above your character level to nudge you to replaying one of the maps you've already completed as a story-less hunt for monsters. Yes, you will have to grind at least a little. Combat is completely action-based. The game feels like it should play like a twin-stick shooter, but doesn't, using the right stick as a directional dodge instead, and mapping normal attacks to the A button. This never sat right with me (especially since I chose the bow as my weapon), and using the same button attacks and interactions seems like a rookie mistake since I often found myself opening chests or worse, drinking one-use health cauldrons in the middle of a fight. It's fun-ish rather than fun, with the difficulty on the average setting being pitched a little bit low and enemies taking a bit too long to die, especially if you're underlevelled. So your character isn't really in any danger of dying most of the time, but progress is a bit of a slog. There's also an environmental exposure mechanic - you're almost always freezing, being poisoned or... overheating? to death, and need to find safe spots to bring the danger gauge down. This adds some sorely needed urgency to your forays, but also hurts the flow of the game even further as you're forced to retreat to a shelter and wait to recover. This may be fixed with higher difficulties or different weapons - I didn't enjoy the game's fundamentals enough to give them a try. Combat feels ponderous, even though it tries to focus on mobility with shielded enemies that need to be surrounded and heavily telegraphed attacks to dodge. It felt to me like they didn't get the balance right. There's a fair amount of character customization; you've got equipment, stats, and perks. there's... five? types of weapons, each one associated to a god with His or Her own skill tree consisting of passive and active skills. Pretty standard stuff, but solid. Everything ties directly to combat or survival, though a little too much of it consists of slight percentage increases to your stats. It's got graphics. Yup. Lots of them. The music is rather nice. The story is fun and completely forgettable. It for some reason casts the Vanir as angels, with the Romans serving them, and the Celts as a different tribes of Vikings (non-Wolf of Midgard division). Like much of the rest of the game, it's happy dumbing things down and being serviceable rather than kicking things up a notch. And that, sadly, is the final impression I took from the game. Really liked how the story ends, so there is that, though the final boss fight was absolute rubbish.

title: Vikings - Wolves of Midgard
text: Vikings -  Wolves of Midgard This game is a traditional Hack'n Slay and is clearly following in the tradition of the Diablo games. ------------------- The gameplay is not very varied. It's basically just your character slashing away on your way through a not so open terrain. Given there are deserts, gloomy windy beaches, coves, and so on. The fact that sometimes you also have to fight against the cold or toxic gas in these levels, adds a nice twist. One great innovation is that you can build up "your" village step by step with various materials that can be looted throughout the levels ( wood, iron, ..). Later on you will also find e.g. runesmiths in your village that will help you on your journey by enchanting your weapons. Big Bonus points for being able to play through the game in co-op. GREAT !! I enjoyed the musical score here, it's well played and adds a lot to the immersion and atmosphere of the game. The sounds of the attacking trolls, their animals or enemy soldiers  are quite realistic as well. Sweet :) The difficulty is set rather low, so I would suggest if you are an avid gamer, that you choose hard for your first playthrough. Normal to me feels like easy. text: Vindictus caught my eye immediately because the gameplay and graphics. Gameplay is smooth, and flows easily. Combat is brutal and efficient. title: Vindictus
text: Its very much a "Its alright.. could be better" kind of game. -Gameplay is decent, although it could be improved, many mechanics just feel thrown in as a gimmick rather than being actually useful. -The controls are janky and sometimes annoying. -The camera would be better if your characters attacks weren't locked to it, I've had few collision issues which is good. -Visually its quite generic, I've had quite a few frame drops during combat which gets annoying. -Customization is insanely limited. You can barely customize your character and considering that is something I love to do.. its definitely a point taker. -Interactions and general exploration is limited and weirdly done. It feels like its trying to be an action-RPG like warframe or Path of Exile but has a bunch of extra UI elements that really dont need to be there. -As for UI/HUD, its quite basic, only really annoying when "in buildings" or trying to access different areas. Generally it has some interesting ideas, the 3rd person action-RPG style is cool and I'd like to see it done more, however the game seems to fail to actually deliver it in a really engaging way. Whether its Nexons fault or lack of enough production time is unkown to me, whatever the case may be its definitely something to look at, however I wouldn't spend money on it.
